reply.overview: This Naya deck is built around Dinosaurs and big creatures that cheat each other into play. [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] smashes in to put Dinosaurs onto the battlefield for free, while cost reducers and ramp get giant threats out early. Enrage triggers from creatures like [[Ripjaw Raptor]] and [[Polyraptor]] snowball value once combat damage starts flying, and the deck closes games through overwhelming trample damage.

strategy: Ramp with pieces like [[Topiary Stomper]] and [[Ranging Raptors]] to accelerate into big threats.
Deploy cost-reducing Dinosaurs such as [[Otepec Huntmaster]] and [[Knight of the Stampede]] to flood the board early.
Attack with [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] to cascade more Dinosaurs directly onto the battlefield.
Trigger Enrage abilities on creatures like [[Trapjaw Tyrant]] and [[Silverclad Ferocidons]] for extra value in combat.
Finish with trample-heavy attackers like [[Ghalta, Primal Hunger]] and [[The Tarrasque]] punching through for lethal damage.

keep: A hand with early ramp like [[Atzocan Seer]] into a mid-curve Dinosaur is ideal.
Keep hands that can deploy [[Knight of the Stampede]] or [[Otepec Huntmaster]] early to cut costs.
sendBack: A hand needing [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] on turn 8 with no other plan falls behind.

tips.text: [[Marauding Raptor]] pings [[Polyraptor]] on entry, triggering Enrage to make a token copy.
[[Forerunner of the Empire]] entering under [[Marauding Raptor]] takes damage and pings the board further.
[[Fight Rigging]] counters build toward a power 7 creature, unlocking its hideaway card for free, and pairs well with cheap [[Thrasta, Tempest's Roar]].
[[Walking Ballista]] can ping [[Bellowing Aegisaur]] to trigger Enrage and spread counters across the team.

keyCards.job: Puts Dinosaurs onto the battlefield on combat damage.
Fetches a basic land whenever it takes damage.
Draws a card whenever it is damaged.
Makes copies of itself when damaged repeatedly.
Exiles an opposing creature when it is damaged.
Pings entering creatures to set off Enrage chains.
Costs little late in a turn, attacks with haste immediately.
Discovers free spells whenever a Dinosaur enters.

weaknesses: The deck leans on attacking with big creatures, so board wipes or fog effects can stall its plan.
Many payoffs depend on [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] connecting in combat, so removal or chump blockers on it hurt badly.
Mana costs skew high, so a hand without early ramp can fall behind on board development.

reply.overview: This five-color Avatar Aang deck builds around bending triggers and Lesson spells to chain card draw, grow lands into creatures via earthbend, and eventually flip Avatar Aang into Aang, Master of Elements for a huge life and card swing plus damage to every opponent. Allies, Shrines, and ramp creatures provide the mana and bodies to support a constant stream of exiled-and-recast spells and incremental board growth.

strategy: Ramp early with mana dorks and rocks to reach five mana for [[Avatar Aang]].
Cast Lesson spells and trigger bending abilities to draw cards off [[Avatar Aang]].
Use earthbend effects to animate lands into threats while building toward all four bending types in one turn.
Transform [[Avatar Aang]] into [[Aang, Master of Elements]] for a burst of life, cards, and damage.
Close games with Ally tokens, Shrine value, and bent-up attackers backed by [[Katara, Water Tribe's Hope]] pumps.

keep: A hand with [[Sol Ring]] or another early ramp piece into a turn-four [[Avatar Aang]].
A hand with a cheap Lesson spell and a way to keep drawing cards.
sendBack: A hand full of expensive bending payoffs with no early plays.
A hand that can't reach five mana by the late turns.

tips.text: [[Energybending]] lets lands gain all basic types, enabling bending triggers that draw cards off [[Avatar Aang]].
Casting [[Earthbending Lesson]] triggers [[Toph, Hardheaded Teacher]] for an extra counter on the earthbent land.
[[Guru Pathik]] finds Shrine cards like [[Crescent Island Temple]], then grows creatures when you cast them.
Counters from attacks let [[Iroh, Dragon of the West]] and [[Jeong Jeong, the Deserter]] generate extra firebending mana.

keyCards.card: Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements
keyCards.job: Draws cards off bending and flips into a finisher.
Grows lands and returns spent instants or sorceries.
Finds Lesson, Saga, or Shrine cards early.
Lowers Lesson spell costs and adds firebending mana.
Builds Monk tokens alongside other Shrines.
Turns small creatures into a unified attack force.
Grows and draws cards off opponents' searches.
Provides any color once Lessons fill the graveyard.

weaknesses: Relies on resolving several bending triggers in one turn to flip the commander, which can be disrupted.
Many lands become creatures and are vulnerable to removal aimed at the land itself.
Lacks hard removal, leaning on earthbend or combat tricks instead.

reply.overview: Kilo, Apogee Mind leads a Jeskai artifact-counters deck built around proliferate triggers and charge counters snowballing into card draw, damage, and extra turns. Artifacts tap for value, counters multiply through proliferate engines like [[Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus]] and [[Deepglow Skate]], and payoffs like [[Lux Artillery]], [[Magistrate's Scepter]], and [[Insight Engine]] close games once counters pile up.

strategy: Deploy cheap artifacts and mana rocks to build an artifact board state early.
Tap [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] to trigger proliferate, growing counters on every permanent that has them.
Use proliferate payoffs like [[Insight Engine]] and [[Tezzeret's Gambit]] to draw extra cards.
Double counters with [[Deepglow Skate]] or copy proliferate with [[Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus]] for big swings.
Finish with [[Lux Artillery]] damage, [[Magistrate's Scepter]] extra turns, or [[Walking Ballista]] counters.

keep: An early artifact into [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] on curve at three mana.
A hand with [[Sol Ring]] or another of the 12 ramp pieces plus a follow-up play.
sendBack: [[Sol Ring]] with nothing to cast after it stalls out.
A hand lacking any proliferate or counter payoff to build toward.

tips.text: Doubling counters with [[Deepglow Skate]] then proliferating twice via [[Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus]] rapidly escalates counters.
[[Zirda, the Dawnwaker]] cheapens activated abilities, letting you tap [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] into proliferate more easily.
[[Power Conduit]] can move a counter onto [[Magistrate's Scepter]] to speed toward an extra turn.
[[Freed from the Real]] on a blue creature combines with [[Unctus, Grand Metatect]] to loop tap triggers for cards.

keyCards.job: Proliferates whenever it becomes tapped.
Doubles every proliferate trigger in the deck.
Instantly doubles counters on chosen permanents.
Builds toward granting an extra turn.
Deals mass damage once counters reach thirty.
Grows into a large card draw engine.
Scales with counters to snipe targets.
Cheapens activated abilities across the board.

weaknesses: Relies heavily on counters accumulating slowly before payoffs come online.
Vulnerable to artifact-hate or counter-removal effects like exile-based removal.
Needs the commander tapped repeatedly to function, so removal on Kilo hurts the plan.

reply.overview: A colorless Eldrazi-artifact ramp deck built around [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]], which grants double cascade to big colorless spells. It floods the board with mana rocks and lands to cast expensive Eldrazi and artifacts early, chaining cascades into more cascades for card advantage and board control, eventually overwhelming opponents with Annihilator creatures, mass exile effects, and resilient artifact threats.

strategy: Play mana rocks and colorless lands early to accelerate toward seven-mana spells.
Cast [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] to turn big colorless spells into cascade chains.
Use mass exile effects like [[All Is Dust]] or [[Ugin, the Spirit Dragon]] to clear boards favoring your resilient artifacts.
Finish with Annihilator creatures such as [[It That Betrays]] or [[Artisan of Kozilek]] grinding opponents out of resources.
Rebuild with card draw engines like [[Mystic Forge]] and [[Hedron Archive]] if the board gets reset.

keep: A hand with early ramp like [[Sol Ring]] plus a way to keep casting spells.
A curve into [[Mind Stone]] or [[Thran Dynamo]] backed by card draw.
sendBack: [[Sol Ring]] with nothing to cast after it stalls out.
A hand with no path to seven mana for big colorless spells.

tips.text: Casting [[Artisan of Kozilek]] off cascade from [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] can reanimate a creature for free value.
[[Mystic Forge]] lets you cast [[Mind Stone]] straight off the top of your library for extra mana.
[[Forsaken Monument]] pumps colorless creatures while [[Skittering Cicada]] grows further whenever you cast colorless spells.
[[Spine of Ish Sah]] returns to hand when it dies, letting you recast it to destroy another permanent, synergizing with cheap [[Metalwork Colossus]] recursion.

keyCards.job: Grants double cascade to big colorless spells.(6)
Forces opponents to sacrifice colored permanents.
Exiles colored permanents and refills your hand.
Steals sacrificed permanents while attacking with Annihilator.
Lets you cast artifacts straight off the library.
Boosts colorless creatures and doubles colorless mana.
Destroys a permanent and returns for reuse.
Generates large bursts of colorless mana.

weaknesses: Relies heavily on expensive spells, so early disruption to mana rocks can slow the whole plan.
Color hate or targeted artifact removal can strip away key engines like [[Mystic Forge]].
The deck can stumble if it fails to hit seven mana for its top-end payoffs.

reply.overview: This mono-Red Goblin deck rallies around [[Krenko, Mob Boss]], flooding the board with Goblin tokens and converting that swarm into direct damage through sacrifice outlets, burn spells, and anthem effects. Once [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] gets even one untapped activation, the Goblin count can explode, letting [[Goblin War Strike]] or a wide alpha strike close the game quickly, while cards like [[Guttersnipe]] and [[Sparksmith]] punish opponents along the way.

strategy: Ramp out early mana with [[Sol Ring]], [[Arcane Signet]], or [[Skirk Prospector]] to deploy [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] on time.
Protect and untap [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] to multiply Goblins exponentially each turn.
Use [[Goblin Warchief]] and [[Goblin Chieftain]] to make the swarm cheap, hasty, and threatening.
Convert extra Goblins into damage via [[Goblin Bombardment]], [[Tar Pitcher]], or [[Goblin War Strike]].
Clear blockers with burn spells like [[Lightning Bolt]] and [[Pinpoint Avalanche]] before attacking.

keep: A hand that curves into [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] on turn 4 with a Goblin to follow.
Early ramp like [[Skirk Prospector]] or [[Mind Stone]] backed by a payoff.
sendBack: A hand full of high-cost burn with no path to Goblins.

tips.text: Tap [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] for tokens, then sacrifice extras to [[Goblin Bombardment]] for reach.
[[Goblin Warchief]] gives every Goblin haste, so tokens from [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] can attack immediately.
Casting [[Firebolt]] and its flashback both trigger [[Guttersnipe]] for extra damage to opponents.
Sacrifice tokens from [[Mogg War Marshal]] to [[Skirk Prospector]] for mana while still getting a death trigger.

keyCards.job: Creates an army of Goblin tokens each turn..
Turns spare Goblins into direct damage..
Discounts Goblins and grants them haste..
Pumps and hastes the Goblin horde..
Pings for damage whenever Goblins die..
Punishes opponents for spells cast..
Turns extra Goblins into mana..
Ramps early, cashes in for a card later..

weaknesses: Board wipes devastate a deck built around wide token swarms.
Krenko, Mob Boss dying before it untaps can leave the plan stalled.
Few ways to interact with noncreature permanents outside artifact removal.

reply.overview: This Jeskai deck leans on a cluster of Gods that gain experience counters and grow threats through proliferate and +1/+1 counter synergies. [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] build up experience counters whenever Gods attack or die, letting Kratos pile counters onto a creature each end step while Atreus refills your hand and burns opponents. Proliferate engines like [[Inexorable Tide]], [[Tezzeret's Gambit]], and [[Flux Channeler]] push counters further, while devotion Gods like [[Purphoros, God of the Forge]] and [[Keranos, God of Storms]] provide steady value and damage until the board overwhelms the table.

strategy: Land both [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] to start generating experience counters.
Attack with Gods to trigger Kratos and accumulate experience counters quickly.
Use proliferate effects like [[Inexorable Tide]] and [[Tezzeret's Gambit]] to grow counters further.
Pour counters into a single threat each end step via Kratos's ability to close games.
Use [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] to refill your hand and ping opponents with accumulated experience.

keep: A hand with early ramp like [[Sol Ring]] or [[Arcane Signet]] into a turn 3 or 4 Kratos.
A hand that curves into a God and has a proliferate spell to follow up.
sendBack: A hand with no path to casting either commander by turn 4.
A hand full of high cost spells with no early plays before turn 3.

tips.text: Casting any spell with [[Inexorable Tide]] out proliferates experience counters, feeding Kratos's end step counter pile faster.
Casting [[Tezzeret's Gambit]] with [[Flux Channeler]] out draws two cards and proliferates twice, snowballing counters quickly.
[[God-Eternal Oketra]] making Zombie tokens triggers [[Purphoros, God of the Forge]] for repeated damage to each opponent.
Recast [[Jeska's Will]] from the graveyard via [[Underworld Breach]] for another burst of mana and card selection.

keyCards.job: Builds experience counters and funnels them to a creature.
Refills hand and pings opponents using experience counters.
Punishes opponents whenever a creature enters.
Proliferates on every spell cast for steady growth.
Cheats creatures into play attacking for free.
Generates Treasure tokens whenever opponents draw cards.
Creates an army of Rebel tokens on attack.
Clears the board of small creatures cheaply.

weaknesses: Relies heavily on accumulating experience counters, which can be slow if Kratos or Atreus is removed early.
Many threats are legendary Gods, so devotion requirements can leave them as noncreatures for a while.
Lacks dedicated mass land disruption, making it vulnerable to decks that race on the ground quickly.

reply.overview: This mono-Blue Wizards control deck casts cheap instants and sorceries, countering threats and drawing extra cards off [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]], [[Azami, Lady of Scrolls]], and other engines. It grinds opponents out of resources before closing with mill-based wins through [[Jace, Wielder of Mysteries]] or [[Laboratory Maniac]], or simply by attrition.

strategy: Play cheap spell-cost reducers like [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] and [[Jace's Sanctum]] early.
Counter key threats with cards like [[Counterspell]] and [[Mana Leak]] while drawing extras.
Build card advantage with [[Azami, Lady of Scrolls]] and [[Diviner's Wand]] off Wizard taps.
Deplete your own library safely, then win with [[Jace, Wielder of Mysteries]] or [[Laboratory Maniac]].
Use bounce and counter loops with [[Ghostly Flicker]] and [[Sea Gate Stormcaller]] to grind value.

keep: A hand with [[Preordain]] or [[Ponder]] to smooth early draws.
A hand holding a counterspell like [[Mana Leak]] alongside a land or two.
sendBack: [[Sol Ring]] with nothing to cast after it stalls out.
A hand lacking any way to interact before turn 2.

tips.text: Flicker [[Mind Stone]] with [[Ghostly Flicker]] to reset its sacrifice ability for another draw.
Flash in [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] to copy [[Sublime Epiphany]] for extra countered spells and card draws.
Equip [[Diviner's Wand]] to [[Azami, Lady of Scrolls]] so her draws grow her power and add flying.
Use [[Vendilion Clique]] to strip a threat while milling yourself toward [[Jace, Wielder of Mysteries]]'s win.

keyCards.job: Cheapens spells and refills your hand on counters.
Converts Wizards into repeatable card draw.
Mills and draws toward an alternate win.
Turns an empty library into a win condition.
Resets enter-the-battlefield triggers for value.
Grows a Wizard and enables repeated draws.
Copies instants or sorceries for double effects.
Finds the right counterspell for the moment.

weaknesses: Relies on having countermagic available, so an empty hand leaves it open to threats.
Can be slow to assemble a win condition without steady card flow.
Vulnerable to decks that apply pressure before counters and draw engines online.

reply.overview: This Dimir deck builds around [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]], using cheap unblockable creatures and ninjutsu to sneak in damage while revealing cards off the top of the library to drain opponents' life. Counterspells and removal protect the board while extra-turn spells and card selection push through lethal reveals.

strategy: Play unblockable creatures like [[Tormented Soul]] or [[Slither Blade]] early to enable ninjutsu.
Swap attackers for [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] or other Ninjas via ninjutsu to trigger damage.
Use [[Brainstorm]], [[Ponder]], and [[Dig Through Time]] to find big mana value cards to reveal.
Hold up [[Counterspell]] or [[Dispel]] to protect key threats during opponents' turns.
Close games with extra turns from [[Temporal Mastery]] or [[Time Warp]] stacking Yuriko triggers.

keep: An early unblockable creature alongside [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] access.
A hand with [[Sol Ring]] and a follow-up spell to cast.
sendBack: A hand with no way to enable ninjutsu before turn 3.
A hand clogged with only reactive counterspells and no threats.

tips.text: [[Satoru Umezawa]] gives creatures in hand ninjutsu, letting you cheat [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]]-style damage from any creature.
[[Dimir Infiltrator]] and [[Muddle the Mixture]] both transmute for mana value 2, fetching needed answers.
[[Silver-Fur Master]] pumps [[Mist-Syndicate Naga]] copies, making an expanding unblockable army.
[[Reanimate]] can bring back [[Ink-Eyes, Servant of Oni]] cheaply to steal a creature on its next hit.

keyCards.job: Converts reveals into life loss for opponents.'
Grants ninjutsu to every creature in hand.
Finds any Ninja from the library.
Lets you cast cards off an opponent's library free.
Steals a creature from a graveyard on hit.
Makes unblockable tokens and digs for answers.
Finds a needed card and refills the hand.
Generates Treasure tokens off Ninja hits.

weaknesses: Relies on unblocked creatures connecting, so boards full of flyers or reach can stall the plan.
Few sweepers or board wipes mean wide opposing boards with reach can slip past.
Early interaction is mostly counterspells, leaving the deck light on removal for resolved threats.
